newsitem.title: USA: Temple-Inland accused of misreporting taxes.
newsitem.headline: Temple-Inland accused of misreporting taxes.

text.p: The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission is investigating allegations by a former accountant of Temple-Inland Inc. that the company underpaid its federal income taxes and filed misleading financial reports, the Washington Post reported Tuesday.
The accountant, Jeffrey Smith Ammon, is suing the company for wrongful termination and alleges he was fired for refusing to participate in wrongful activity, according to the report.
Temple-Inland Inc on Monday denied allegations made by employee in the suit, although it did not spell them out.
The company said it was confident that the court would find that the allegations made by the former assistant tax manager had no merit and declined to comment further until the suit's resolution.
Temple-Inland of Diboll, Texas, makes paper, corrugated packaging and building products, with financial services operations in mortgage and consumer banking.

The Washington Post quoted court papers as saying that from 1988 ato 1994, the company understated profits by $75 million in reports to the SEC and shareholders by hiding tax benefits from its acquisition of three failed Texas savings and loans.

In 1990, he alleged the company began claiming hundreds of millions of dollars in improper deductions on its tax returns, which resulted in $80 million to $100 million in underpayments of federal income taxes.
In addition, Ammon alleged that the company concealed tax benefits from the Resolution Trust Corp., the federal agency that had sold it the thrifts and that was supposed to share in the tax savings.
